title: Diomede: See Tomorrow
status: approved by the user 2026-10-31 ("Approve all three"), no edits

lines.text: From this island, you can see tomorrow.
This is Little Diomede. Alaska. Seventy-seven people.
And that's Big Diomede. Russia. Nobody lives there.
The gap between them? Three point eight kilometres.
Pull back, and the reason is a line.
The border runs right down the middle. And so does the International Date Line.
Monday lunchtime here is Tuesday morning there.
In the Cold War, this gap had a name. The Ice Curtain.
Then, in 1987, a swimmer named Lynne Cox got in.
Six-degree water. Two hours, six minutes.
She swam across the line. Into tomorrow.
Reagan and Gorbachev both praised her.
Two islands. Three point eight kilometres. Twenty-one hours.
